svg.title: Four Gates Before the Definitive License Closes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-license-clause-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Gates Before the Definitive License Closes; subtitle: Scope, performance, indexation and reversion checks; caption: Operators lock the commercial skeleton in a short term sheet, then fight over scope, money and exit triggers; royalties typically land at 3 to 7% with 5% as the anchor.; assumptions note: Term sheets are treated as non-binding except for exclusivity, no-shop and confidentiality. Industry royalty bands run 0.1 to 25% per UpCounsel, so the 5% anchor moves with category, leverage and market proof.; note: Attributed to Ayers Law TV (Andrew M. Ayers), J.D. Houvener of Bold Patents Law Firm, Bao Tran, BaxterIPAttorneys, a Boardgame Publisher and Licensing Basics (Ryan Stewart).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does the grant language state exclusive, sole or non-exclusive?; pass next: G2; fail action: Rewrite the grant; discovering a non-exclusive license later leaves no way to stop a competitor.; gate: G2; question: Does every exclusive grant carry a performance clause?; pass next: G3; fail action: Add an explicit right to terminate on a missed milestone, separate from good-faith renegotiation.; gate: G3; question: Is every per-unit or foreign-currency royalty indexed?; pass next: G4; fail action: Provide for proper indexation, since a fixed foreign-currency royalty can lose badly.; gate: G4; question: Are reversion triggers written for bankruptcy, ceasing to operate and out-of-print status?; pass next: Close the definitive license; fail action: Hold the closing until automatic reversion triggers are in.

text.title: Four Gates Before the Definitive License Closes
text.tspan: Four Gates Before the Definitive License Closes

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does the grant language state exclusive, sole or non-exclusive?; pass next: G2; fail action: Rewrite the grant; discovering a non-exclusive license later leaves no way to stop a competitor.

gate: G2; question: Does every exclusive grant carry a performance clause?; pass next: G3; fail action: Add an explicit right to terminate on a missed milestone, separate from good-faith renegotiation.
gate: G3; question: Is every per-unit or foreign-currency royalty indexed?; pass next: G4; fail action: Provide for proper indexation, since a fixed foreign-currency royalty can lose badly.

gate: G4; question: Are reversion triggers written for bankruptcy, ceasing to operate and out-of-print status?; pass next: Close the definitive license; fail action: Hold the closing until automatic reversion triggers are in.

text.title: Assumptions: Term sheets are treated as non-binding except for exclusivity, no-shop and confidentiality. Industry royalty bands run 0.1 to 25% per UpCounsel, so the 5% anchor moves with category, leverage and market proof.
